Reportedly, Apple's annual sales in India for the last fiscal year surpassed US$10 billion for the first time.

With the country's per capita annual income under US$3,000, this is no small feat—especially given iPhones are priced higher in India than in the US…

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But in recent years, with local economic growth and Apple finally opening Apple Stores in the country, the situation has changed considerably.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given the low per capita income locally and that iPhones are manufactured in India, you might assume prices there would be much lower than in the US. In reality, however, due to high taxes, Apple products are priced higher in India than in the US.

Apple has tried to offset the difference in part by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently about a quarter of iPhones are produced in India, but most are sold to the US market. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements specifically to avoid US tariffs on Chinese imports.
